ted-w-lieu.text: Voted Nay on H.R. 1 (the 2025 reconciliation bill, later enacted as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act) when the House passed it on May 22, 2025, and voted No again on the Senate-amended version on July 3, 2025.

source.title: GovTrack: H.R. 1 House passage, May 22, 2025 (House roll call)

ted-w-lieu.text: Sponsor of the Climate Solutions Act of 2025 (H.R. 6098), introduced Nov. 18, 2025, whose stated purpose is "to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and protect the climate."

source.title: GovTrack: H.R. 6098 Climate Solutions Act of 2025

ted-w-lieu.text: Sponsor of the Increasing Penalties for Offshore Polluters Act (H.R. 3071), which would increase civil and criminal penalties for oil spills under the Federal Water Pollution Control Act.

source.title: GovTrack: H.R. 3071 Increasing Penalties for Offshore Polluters Act

ted-w-lieu.text: Sponsor of the Housing for All Act of 2025 (H.R. 2945), "to address the homelessness and housing crises, to move toward the goal of providing for a home for all Americans."

source.title: GovTrack: H.R. 2945 Housing for All Act of 2025

ted-w-lieu.text: Sponsor of the Prevent Homelessness Act of 2025 (H.R. 2206), to create a Housing Stabilization Fund providing emergency housing assistance to extremely low-income renters and homeowners.

source.title: GovTrack: H.R. 2206 Prevent Homelessness Act of 2025

ted-w-lieu.text: Original cosponsor of the Medicare for All Act (H.R. 3069), per GovTrack's cosponsor list.

source.title: GovTrack: H.R. 3069 Medicare for All Act cosponsors

ted-w-lieu.text: Voted Yea on H.R. 1834 (Jan. 8, 2026), a bill to reinstate enhanced Affordable Care Act subsidies for three years; it passed 230-196.

source.title: GovTrack: H.R. 1834 ACA subsidies (House roll call)

ted-w-lieu.text: Sponsor of the Reproductive Data Privacy and Protection Act (H.R. 3218), to ensure data requests on individuals do not pertain to reproductive services; also an original cosponsor of the Women's Health Protection Act (H.R. 12) and Equality Act (H.R. 15).

source.title: GovTrack: H.R. 3218 Reproductive Data Privacy and Protection Act

ted-w-lieu.text: Voted Nay on the Laken Riley Act (H.R. 29) on Jan. 7, 2025, and Nay on the Senate version (S. 5) on Jan. 22, 2025.

source.title: GovTrack: H.R. 29 Laken Riley Act (House roll call)

ted-w-lieu.text: Voted Nay on the SAVE Act (H.R. 22), April 10, 2025, and Nay on S. 1383, the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act, Feb. 11, 2026.

source.title: GovTrack: H.R. 22 SAVE Act (House roll call)

ted-w-lieu.text: Voted Nay on H.Con.Res. 96, "Expressing support for law enforcement officers" (May 13, 2026), and Yea on the Cashless Bail Reporting Act (H.R. 5625, May 14, 2026).

source.title: GovTrack: H.Con.Res. 96 support for law enforcement officers (House roll call)

ted-w-lieu.text: Voted Nay on the Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act (H.R. 1041), May 21, 2026; it passed 216-201.

source.title: GovTrack: H.R. 1041 Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act (House roll call)

ted-w-lieu.text: Voted Nay on the Affordable HOMES Act (H.R. 5184) on Jan. 9, 2026; it passed 263-147.

source.title: GovTrack: H.R. 5184 Affordable HOMES Act (House roll call)

ted-w-lieu.text: Voted Nay on the Unlocking our Domestic LNG Potential Act (H.R. 1949), Nov. 20, 2025; it passed 217-188.

source.title: GovTrack: H.R. 1949 Unlocking our Domestic LNG Potential Act (House roll call)

ted-w-lieu.text: Ballotpedia lists his 2026 endorsements as including the California Federation of Labor Unions AFL-CIO, California Teachers Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters, Sierra Club Angeles Chapter and Equality California.

source.title: Ted Lieu - Ballotpedia

houston-brignano.text: Wants "a fair immigration system where Native-born citizens get the first shot at jobs," with no "back door deals or secret amnesty." Calls for strong borders, thorough vetting, and removing criminals.

source.title: Solutions - Houston Brignano for Congress

houston-brignano.text: Supports portable health savings accounts, cross-state insurance competition, price transparency, and giving people "thousands of choices" of provider, starting with local institutions rather than a "top-down model."

source.title: Solutions - Houston Brignano for Congress

houston-brignano.text: Says high housing costs are "a political failure" and proposes innovation zones for technology, manufacturing and energy, plus streamlining regulations. States "regulations restrict new development, driving up costs."

source.title: Houston Brignano - Ballotpedia (2025 Candidate Connection survey)

houston-brignano.text: Would cut regulation by controlling presidential overreach through the REINS Act, so "inventors and businesses grow without heavy burdens," and cut bureaucracies that slow aid and raise costs.

source.title: Solutions - Houston Brignano for Congress

houston-brignano.text: Proposes tax breaks for buying homes or starting companies, more job training, and fixing the student loan crisis; wants to stop "waste, fraud, and abuse in government spending."

source.title: Solutions - Houston Brignano for Congress

houston-brignano.text: Cites $882 billion a year in federal debt interest and pledges to publish every meeting, donor and vote explanation online. Says: "No backroom deals. No corporate PAC money."

source.title: Houston Brignano - Ballotpedia (2025 Candidate Connection survey)

houston-brignano.text: Says to "trust the American people with choice whether that's housing, healthcare, or education." Gives no more detailed education platform on his site.

source.title: Houston Brignano - Ballotpedia (2025 Candidate Connection survey)

houston-brignano.text: Says young people should be trained "to master" AI "instead of fearing it." Supports "smart safeguards" but opposes "bureaucratic paralysis that hands dominance to our adversaries."

source.title: Houston Brignano - Ballotpedia (2025 Candidate Connection survey)

notes: Incumbent evidence is from GovTrack House roll-call and bill pages (house.gov and clerk.house.gov blocked automated fetches). Brignano's site is general; no stated positions found on policing, homelessness, guns, climate, abortion or transportation.
